text:
Drake Batherson has been one of Ottawa's steadiest scorers, a former fourth-round pick with 10 goals and 19 points in 21 games at 17:41 a night. The Senators have won six of their last ten, and his goal against Colorado on Nov. 12 ended a scoring drought (CBS Sports) on a night he put six shots on net.

The finishing is the question. Ten goals on 7.1 expected means he's shooting 21%, close to last season's 20%, but that rate rarely holds for anyone. Last year ran the other way: Evolving-Hockey had him at 2.8 expected wins against 1.5 actual. So some of this season is the bill coming due in his favour.

His five-on-five game is better than his shot-attempt numbers suggest: Ottawa takes only 47.6% of attempts with him on, but 54.2% of the expected goals, which means the chances they do get are good ones. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 89th percentile for primary shot assists last season. What to watch: shots. He has 48 in 21 games. If the finishing cools without more volume, the goals will slow.
headline: Batherson's finishing is doing the heavy lifting
